headline: DOE COMMITS $2.7B TO DOMESTIC ENRICHMENT — HALEU Now US-Only Fuel; Urenco, ACO, General Matter Target SMR Fuel Chain By 2027
snippet: A September 4 market assessment finds the US Department of Energy has committed $2.7 billion to build domestic low-enriched and high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) infrastructure, with $900 million task orders each to American Centrifuge Operating and General Matter running 10 years, as Urenco received NRC authorization in October 2025 to produce LEU+ with first deliveries to a fuel fabricator now underway in 2026. The report underscores that nuclear fuel security requires coordinated investment across the entire fuel cycle — not just mined uranium — accelerating demand for US domestic feedstock from conventional mines and in-situ recovery operations, with HALEU being the only viable fuel for next-generation SMRs currently produced commercially only in Russia.

headline: CHINA ALONE BLOCKS ANGLO TECK — World's 5th Largest Copper Miner One Approval Away; 11-Day Close Window Set; US$4.5B Dividend Mechanics Confirmed
snippet: China remained the sole outstanding regulatory jurisdiction blocking the Anglo American–Teck Resources merger of equals as of August 19, with the September 2026–March 2027 closing window intact and all other approvals secured. Teck's September 1 disclosure sets the final closing mechanics: once China clears, an eleven-trading-day window runs to effectiveness at 1.3301 Anglo shares per Teck share, Anglo pays a US$4.5 billion special dividend ($4.19/share) within 30 days, and existing Anglo holders own 62.4% of Anglo Teck — the world's fifth-largest copper producer targeting US$800 million in annual synergies from headcount, procurement, and capital allocation improvements.

headline: VALE DROPS CRITICAL MINERALS IPO — Brazilian Nationalism Kills Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Listing; VBM Stays Private Indefinitely
snippet: Vale has indefinitely shelved the initial public offering of Vale Base Metals Ltd. — its copper, nickel, and cobalt subsidiary with assets across Canada, Brazil, Japan, Britain, and Indonesia — after the Lula government pushed back on ceding control of strategic mineral assets to public markets. The IPO was targeted for mid-2026 as recently as March, with VBM CEO Shaun Usmar having signalled the unit was on track; the cancellation removes a significant pricing catalyst for junior copper and nickel developers that had expected the IPO to reset comparable-company valuations in the sector.

headline: SOUTHERN CROSS GOLD DRILLS 972 g/t AU AT 808m DEPTH — Sunday Creek Apollo 9th-Best Intersection All-Time; Easternmost Extension Confirmed In Victoria
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated Ltd. (TSX: SXGC | ASX: SX2) reported September 2 that hole SDDSC222W1 at the Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria returned 0.6 m grading 993.2 g/t AuEq (972.0 g/t Au, 8.9% Sb) from 808.5 m — the 9th-highest composite intersection across 142.5 km of drilling at Sunday Creek, 620 m below surface. Step-out holes simultaneously pushed the Apollo East zone to its furthest eastern extent yet; Sunday Creek has now logged 98 composite intersections exceeding 100 g/t Au across 283 holes, consolidating its position as one of the highest-grade gold-antimony systems drilled in Australia.

headline: BEZANT RESOURCES HITS FIRST BLAST, FIRST ORE AT HOPE & GOROB — 130 On Site; September Copper Concentrate; Hartree-Backed Namibia Project Goes Live
snippet: Bezant Resources (LSE: BZT) confirmed its Hope & Gorob copper-gold project in Namibia has completed its first two production blasts and is stockpiling run-of-mine ore ahead of processing through the Tsoaxaub Metals Processing Plant in September 2026, transitioning from construction into operations. With 130 employees and contractors on site, mechanical installation of flotation cells, crushers, and the assay lab nearing completion, and a Hartree-backed US$7 million financing package covering working capital through first concentrate, Bezant becomes the first new copper concentrate producer in Namibia's Khomas Hochland region in several years.

headline: STANMORE SNAPS UP MORANBAH SOUTH FROM EXXARO FOR US$105M — 743 Mt Met Coal Resource; Eagle Downs Synergies; Q4 2026 Close
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) agreed in early September 2026 to acquire Exxaro Resources' Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland — holding 743 million tonnes of resources — for US$105 million cash, conditional on Exxaro first exercising its preemption right over Anglo American's 50% joint venture stake. Completion is expected before year-end Q4 2026 using existing liquidity with no shareholder vote required; Moranbah South's adjacency to Stanmore's Eagle Downs mine creates direct infrastructure-sharing potential across one of Queensland's richest hard coking coal corridors.
